boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain St Lawrence University
boards.description: Verified evening food stops on campus and around Canton, with current availability noted for each.

cards.title: Crave Cafe
cards.subtitle: 67 Main Street, Canton
cards.notes: Use the Saturday after-midnight pickup window when it fits your plans; confirm ordering availability before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street option with a listed Saturday window into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Crave Cafe’s official Toast ordering page lists Saturday hours of 12:00 a.m.–2:15 a.m. and identifies the location as 67 Main Street, Canton.
cards.source_title: Crave Cafe online ordering and hours
cards.access_notes: Listed Saturday hours are 12:00 a.m.–2:15 a.m.; check the live ordering page before going.

cards.title: Northstar Café
cards.subtitle: Sullivan Student Center, St. Lawrence University
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of the Student Center for a campus-based food stop; check Dining Services for the day’s service details.
cards.short_summary: The campus café identified by St. Lawrence as opening early and staying open late.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence University states that Northstar Café is on the lower level of the Sullivan Student Center and “opens early, stays open late.”
cards.source_title: Dining | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: The university describes it as staying open late but does not publish a specific closing time on this page; verify current service before visiting.

cards.title: The Corner
cards.subtitle: Pi Nu Epsilon Atrium, Chaney Dining Center, SUNY Canton
cards.notes: For an evening food run, use the Sunday–Thursday late-night program at Chaney Dining Center and check campus status first.
cards.short_summary: A nearby campus late-night program with pizza, calzones, sandwiches, and drinks.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Canton lists The Corner’s Sunday–Thursday late-night program from 8:00 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. in the Pi Nu Epsilon Atrium at Chaney Dining Center.
cards.source_title: Hours and Locations | SUNY Canton
cards.access_notes: Listed Sunday–Thursday hours are 8:00–10:30 p.m.; access is on the SUNY Canton campus.

cards.title: Parkway Express Canton
cards.subtitle: 5994 US Highway 11, Canton
cards.notes: Use this Route 11 stop for a later convenience-food run; check the store directly if a holiday or weather event affects service.
cards.short_summary: A Canton convenience stop whose operator lists daily evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Parkway Express identifies its Canton location at 5994 US Highway 11 and lists daily hours of 6:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: Parkway Express contact and locations
cards.access_notes: Operator-listed hours are Sunday–Saturday, 6:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.

cards.title: 11 West
cards.subtitle: 6182 US-11, Canton
cards.notes: Plan around the dinner service rather than bar hours, and confirm the kitchen is serving before making the trip north of campus.
cards.short_summary: A Canton restaurant with dinner service listed through 9 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: 11 West lists dinner service Tuesday–Sunday from 4:30 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. at 6182 US-11 in Canton.
cards.source_title: 11 West | Canton, NY
cards.access_notes: Restaurant dinner is listed Tuesday–Sunday, 4:30–9:00 p.m.; the venue is closed Mondays.

cards.title: Sergi's Italian Restaurant & Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: 31 Main Street, Canton
cards.notes: Use the Main Street pizzeria during its listed evening service; check the live ordering page before heading downtown.
cards.short_summary: A family-operated Canton pizzeria with nightly service listed until 9 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Sergi’s official ordering page lists 31 Main Street, Canton, with service Monday–Saturday from 4:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: Sergi's Italian Restaurant & Pizzeria online ordering and hours
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Saturday, 4:00–9:00 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: County Seat Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Best Western University Inn, 90 East Main Street, Canton
cards.notes: Choose from the food and nonalcoholic menu at this East Main Street restaurant, then confirm pickup or seating before you go.
cards.short_summary: A restaurant at the University Inn that lists food service until 9 p.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: The County Seat Restaurant’s official Toast page lists its address as 90 East Main Street, Canton, and daily hours of 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: County Seat Restaurant online ordering and hours
cards.access_notes: Listed daily hours are 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.; the official menu includes nonalcoholic beverages.

cards.title: Not Just Sandwiches
cards.subtitle: 5994 U.S. Route 11, Canton
cards.notes: Use the Route 11 pickup option for an evening sandwich, grill, or pizza order, checking the live page for ordering status first.
cards.short_summary: A takeout-focused Canton food counter that lists service through 9 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Not Just Sandwiches’ official Toast page lists its Canton location at 5994 U.S. Route 11 and says it closes at 9 p.m.
cards.source_title: Not Just Sandwiches online ordering and hours
cards.access_notes: The live ordering page lists a 9:00 p.m. close; ordering availability can change.

cards.title: Dana Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: St. Lawrence University campus
cards.notes: Use Dana for an on-campus evening meal and check Dining Services before going, especially during breaks or schedule changes.
cards.short_summary: St. Lawrence’s main dining hall, open every day into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence University states that Dana Dining Hall is open seven days a week from 7:30 a.m. to 8:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Dining | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: University-listed hours are daily, 7:30 a.m.–8:30 p.m.; hours may differ during breaks.

cards.title: Chaney Dining Center
cards.subtitle: SUNY Canton campus
cards.notes: Use Chaney’s continuous evening dining service when it is available, then verify guest and meal-plan access before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A nearby campus dining hall with daily service into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Canton lists Chaney Dining Center hours as 7:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m. Monday–Friday and 10:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m. Saturday–Sunday.
cards.source_title: Hours and Locations | SUNY Canton
cards.access_notes: Listed closing time is 7:30 p.m. every day; verify current campus access and payment arrangements.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces with documented study, gathering, performance, or student-organization uses.

cards.title: Settle into the Cole Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Herring-Cole Hall
cards.notes: Bring quiet work to this designated study room; individual desk work and reading are its documented academic-year use.
cards.short_summary: A historic reading room reserved by tradition for quiet individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence designates the Cole Reading Room in Herring-Cole Hall as quiet study space during the academic year, for individual desk work and reading.
cards.source_title: Room Usage Policy | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Near silence is the stated norm; it may not be reserved for purposes other than individual desk work and reading.

cards.title: Use the MacAllaster Room
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library
cards.notes: Choose this named library study room when you need a dedicated place to work outside the library’s regular spaces.
cards.short_summary: A named 24-hour study space in Owen D. Young Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The St. Lawrence Libraries space directory lists the MacAllaster Room as 'Owen D. Young Library 24-Hour Study.'
cards.source_title: Explore Our Spaces | St. Lawrence University Libraries
cards.access_notes: The library identifies this as a 24-hour study space; verify current building and card-access arrangements before going.

cards.title: Work from the library mezzanine
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library
cards.notes: Use the mezzanine when an open study setting suits your reading, writing, or laptop work; check library access before arrival.
cards.short_summary: An open study area on the mezzanine of Owen D. Young Library.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence Libraries identifies the Mezzanine Study Area in Owen D. Young Library as an open study space.
cards.source_title: Mezzanine Study Area | St. Lawrence University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Listed as open study space in Owen D. Young Library; confirm current library access and availability.

cards.title: Meet in Fox Seminar Room
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library
cards.notes: Check the room calendar, then use this seminar room for group work when it is not reserved for a scheduled class.
cards.short_summary: A library seminar room available for non-reserved student group study.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence Libraries states that ODY 125B, the Fox Seminar Room, is available for non-reserved student group study outside regularly scheduled classes.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Library Space | St. Lawrence University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserved for regularly scheduled classes in coordination with the registrar; otherwise available for non-reserved student group study.

cards.title: Check out ODY 140B
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library
cards.notes: Use the computer lab for shared project work when research and technology instruction are not occupying the room.
cards.short_summary: A library computer lab that also opens for unreserved student group study.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence Libraries says ODY 140B is used for research and technology instruction and is otherwise available for non-reserved student group study.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Library Space | St. Lawrence University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Research and technology instruction has priority; use it for group study only at other times.

cards.title: Gather at Sullivan Student Center
cards.subtitle: Student-centered campus hub
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the student center’s shared areas, keeping in mind that groups can reserve some spaces without closing them off.
cards.short_summary: A wireless-equipped center whose space-use policy gives first priority to students.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence’s room-use policy says student use has first priority in the Sullivan Student Center and identifies shared atrium, campus room, and patio spaces.
cards.source_title: Room Usage Policy | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Some spaces are reservable; the Atrium, Campus Room, and Outdoor Patio cannot be closed off to students, faculty, and staff in the building.

cards.title: Take a break on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Central campus green
cards.notes: Use this documented student space for a daytime pause, informal meetup, or outdoor reading, and route organized requests through Student Activities.
cards.short_summary: A campus green identified by the university as primarily a student space.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence’s room-use policy identifies the Quad as primarily a student space and says use requests are reviewed by Student Activities staff.
cards.source_title: Room Usage Policy | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Organized use requests are reviewed by Student Activities staff; follow current campus guidance for events.

cards.title: Catch a Java House show
cards.subtitle: 5 University Ave.
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled live show at this student-run campus venue; residents help book performers and facilitate programming.
cards.short_summary: A student-run campus entertainment venue where residents help produce live shows.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence Housing describes Java House at 5 University Ave. as an entirely student-run campus entertainment venue where residents book performers and facilitate live shows.
cards.source_title: Housing | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Attend only scheduled programming and follow venue and campus event guidance.

cards.title: Look for an Arts Annex open mic
cards.subtitle: 21 Romoda Dr.
cards.notes: Watch for resident-hosted open mics or stoop shows, then attend the announced program rather than treating the residence as drop-in space.
cards.short_summary: An arts-focused theme house whose members host open mics and front-porch shows.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence Housing says the Arts Annex at 21 Romoda Dr. is home to artists and that members host open mics and 'stoop shows' on its front porch.
cards.source_title: Housing | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: This is a residence; attend announced events and respect residential access and any host instructions.

cards.title: Connect at the Black Student Union
cards.subtitle: 52 Park St.
cards.notes: Engage with the BSU’s advocacy and dialogue programming when invited or scheduled, respecting the organization’s community-centered purpose.
cards.short_summary: A named campus space for Black students and allies focused on advocacy and dialogue.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence Housing identifies the Black Student Union at 52 Park St. as committed to supporting Black students and allies and providing a space for advocacy and dialogue.
cards.source_title: Housing | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Use in accordance with BSU programming, invitations, and residential-access expectations.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase activities at St. Lawrence and in Canton.

cards.title: Browse the Brush Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Griffiths Arts Center · St. Lawrence University
cards.notes: Visit the rotating exhibitions during the academic year; check the gallery page before heading over for the current display and visitor hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery with changing visual-art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence describes the Richard F. Brush Art Gallery as free and open to the public during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Richard F. Brush Art Gallery to Present Exhibition
cards.access_notes: Free public access is stated for the academic year; verify current gallery hours before visiting.

cards.title: Catch a free weekend movie
cards.subtitle: Sullivan Student Center · St. Lawrence University
cards.notes: Look for the weekend film offering in the Student Center and bring a friend; the university specifically lists these movies as free.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost campus movie option held on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence lists attending free movies in the Student Center each weekend among student activities.
cards.source_title: Get Involved
cards.access_notes: Program is presented as a student activity; consult the campus calendar for a specific screening.

cards.title: Walk the campus trail network
cards.subtitle: Nine campus trails · St. Lawrence University
cards.notes: Choose a daylight walk through the university’s campus trails; use the map or Outdoor Program resources to plan a route that fits your time.
cards.short_summary: Nine public campus trails through St. Lawrence grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence states that its nine campus trails are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: St. Lawrence in the Community
cards.access_notes: The university notes that walking trails close at dusk; stay on designated routes.

cards.title: Take the Saddlemire Trail loop
cards.subtitle: Starts behind Hulett and Jencks · St. Lawrence University
cards.notes: Start behind Hulett and Jencks for an easy 2.1-mile route with boardwalks, Tracy Brook, Little River, and views near the golf course.
cards.short_summary: An easy campus trail with boardwalk sections and water features.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence's Outdoor Program identifies Saddlemire Trail as a 2.1-mile easy trail beginning behind Hulett and Jencks dormitories.
cards.source_title: Local Hikes
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required because it is part of the university's free public campus trail network; trails close at dusk.

cards.title: Walk Kip Trail from the field station
cards.subtitle: Wachtmeister Field Station · St. Lawrence University
cards.notes: Begin at Wachtmeister Field Station and follow this easy 2.2-mile campus route; bring water and return before the university’s dusk trail closure.
cards.short_summary: An easy 2.2-mile campus walk from Wachtmeister Field Station.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence's Outdoor Program lists Kip Trail as an easy 2.2-mile route starting at Wachtmeister Field Station.
cards.source_title: Local Hikes
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required because it is part of the university's free public campus trail network; trails close at dusk.

cards.title: Navigate the St. Lawrence Orienteering Course
cards.subtitle: Wachtmeister Field Station near Kip Trail · St. Lawrence University
cards.notes: Download the free map and instructions, then work through the controls with a friend; stay oriented and follow the site’s safety and Leave No Trace guidance.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided navigation course with free maps.
cards.evidence_claim: Nature Up North states that the St. Lawrence Orienteering Course is open to the public and provides free downloadable maps and instructions.
cards.source_title: St. Lawrence Orienteering Course
cards.access_notes: Use daylight, follow the posted navigation advice, and do not cross the Little River.

cards.title: Attend a Writers Series reading
cards.subtitle: Sykes Common Room · 85 Park Street, Canton
cards.notes: Check the Writers Series schedule, then arrive for an author reading and Q&A; the university says these events are free and open to the public.
cards.short_summary: Author readings and questions in Sykes Common Room.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence states that Writers Series author readings are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: About the Writers Series
cards.access_notes: Readings are typically Thursday evenings; confirm the specific event schedule before going.

cards.entity_name: Alison Hawthorne Deming Writers Series Event
cards.title: Hear Alison Hawthorne Deming read
cards.subtitle: Sykes Common Room · October 20, 2026
cards.notes: Plan for the scheduled Writers Series event in Sykes Common Room, then stay for the reading’s conversation with the visiting author.
cards.short_summary: A free public Writers Series event with Alison Hawthorne Deming.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence lists the October 20, 2026 Alison Hawthorne Deming Writers Series event as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Writers Series and the Center for the Environment present Alison Hawthorne Deming
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for October 20, 2026, 8–9 p.m.; verify details on the event page before attending.

cards.entity_name: Shakespeare Theatre of New Jersey at St. Lawrence
cards.title: See free Shakespeare on campus
cards.subtitle: Eben Holden Center · March 12–14, 2027
cards.notes: Save the announced March dates for A Midsummer Night’s Dream or Romeo and Juliet; the university says no tickets are needed.
cards.short_summary: Two announced no-ticket Shakespeare performances at Eben Holden.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence states that its March 12–14, 2027 Shakespeare Theatre of New Jersey performances are free and open to the public with no tickets needed.
cards.source_title: Shakespeare Theatre of New Jersey
cards.access_notes: Performances are scheduled for March 12–14, 2027; confirm the chosen performance time before attending.

cards.entity_name: Performance and Communication Arts Public Events
cards.title: Watch a Performance and Communication Arts event
cards.subtitle: St. Lawrence University · Canton, NY
cards.notes: Use the university events calendar to find a faculty- or student-directed production, showcase, performance hour, lecture, or workshop that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: Public campus performances, lectures, showcases, and workshops.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence's catalog states that Performance and Communication Arts public events, including productions, showcases, lectures, and workshops, are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: St. Lawrence University Catalog 2016–2017
cards.access_notes: Individual events vary; use the current university calendar to confirm date, venue, and any entry requirements.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named study environments documented by St. Lawrence University Libraries, centered on the Owen D. Young Library.

cards.title: Study Area
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library · Lower Level
cards.notes: Set up at a carrel when you want daylight and a computer close at hand; the lower-level area also includes couches and armchairs.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level open study area pairing natural light, carrels, computers, and lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The library describes this lower-level open study space as having natural light, study carrels with computers, and couches/armchairs.
cards.source_title: Study Area | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Owen D. Young Library on the lower level; consult the library hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Tree Room Study Area
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library · Upper Level
cards.notes: Choose a couch or armchair in this open-plan upper-level area when you want to work in a space framing the library’s top floor.
cards.short_summary: An upper-level open study area with soft seating around the Tree Room.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies the Tree Room as an open-plan study area framing ODY’s upper level, with couches and armchairs.
cards.source_title: Tree Room: Study Area | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the upper level of Owen D. Young Library; consult the library hours page before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Study Carrels ODY Lower Level - East
cards.title: East Lower-Level Carrels
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library · Lower Level
cards.notes: Use an individual carrel for focused work, or gather at the central table when a small collaborative session needs nearby power.
cards.short_summary: Ten powered carrels and a central collaboration table in a naturally lit lower-level section.
cards.evidence_claim: The space has 10 study carrels, natural light, power and network connections, plus a large central table for collaborative work.
cards.source_title: Study Carrels ODY Lower Level - East | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level of Owen D. Young Library; consult the library hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Study Alcove
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library · East Side
cards.notes: Head to this east-side alcove for a quieter open-study setting, with couches and armchairs available for settling into a reading block.
cards.short_summary: A quiet east-side alcove with lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The library describes the Study Alcove as a quiet alcove on ODY’s east side with couches and armchairs.
cards.source_title: Study Alcove | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the east side of Owen D. Young Library; consult the library hours page before visiting.

cards.title: MacAllaster 24-Hour Study
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library · Main Level
cards.notes: Use this 45-seat room for group work when it is not reserved; check the reservation calendar before relying on the space.
cards.short_summary: A reservable main-level study room that is otherwise available for non-reserved student group study.
cards.evidence_claim: The MacAllaster Room has 45 seats and is available for non-reserved student group study outside special-event and class reservations.
cards.source_title: 24-Hour Study - MacAllaster Room | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Main level of Owen D. Young Library. It may be reserved for special events or instruction; verify availability before use.

cards.title: Frost Ferguson Library Instruction Room
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library · Room 204, Upper Level
cards.notes: Bring a group and use the projector or whiteboard when the room is unreserved; it returns to student group-study use outside instruction.
cards.short_summary: A 36-seat upper-level group-study and instruction room with presentation tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 204 has 36 seats, a projector/digital display and whiteboard, and is available for non-reserved student group study outside instruction.
cards.source_title: 204 - Frost Ferguson Library Instruction Room | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Upper level of Owen D. Young Library. Used for research and technology instruction; verify that it is not reserved.

cards.title: Upper-Level Tree Room Carrels
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library · Upper Level
cards.notes: Pick one of these Tree Room carrels for individual work that needs power and wired network connections at the desk.
cards.short_summary: Upper-level individual carrels equipped with electrical and network connections.
cards.evidence_claim: The upper-level Tree Room carrels each have an outlet with three sockets and two network connections.
cards.source_title: Study Carrels ODY Upper Level | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located in the Tree Room on the upper level of Owen D. Young Library; consult library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Mezzanine Study Area
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library
cards.notes: Use this named open-study area as a simple change of scenery within ODY; confirm floor access and library hours on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A designated open-study area on the library mezzanine.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence Libraries lists the Mezzanine Study Area as an open study space in Owen D. Young Library.
cards.source_title: Mezzanine Study Area | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Owen D. Young Library; the direct listing does not state additional reservation requirements.

cards.title: Josephine Young Room
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library
cards.notes: Take a large armchair and side table for reading or drafting; this named room is listed among the library’s group-study environments.
cards.short_summary: An elegant reading room furnished with large armchairs and side tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The library describes the Josephine Young Room as an elegant reading room with large armchairs and side tables.
cards.source_title: Group Study | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Owen D. Young Library; the direct listing does not state additional reservation requirements.

cards.title: Hearst Study Area
cards.subtitle: Owen D. Young Library
cards.notes: Use the west-facing group-study area when a reference computer and a bright setting suit the work you need to finish.
cards.short_summary: A bright, west-facing open-study area with a networked reference computer.
cards.evidence_claim: The library describes the Hearst Study Area as a bright, warm west-facing group-study area with a networked reference computer.
cards.source_title: Open Study Space | St. Lawrence University Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Owen D. Young Library; the direct listing does not state additional reservation requirements.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, public-facing Canton destinations along Main Street and Park Street near St. Lawrence University.

cards.title: Borrow, research, or join a program
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor — 8 Park Street
cards.notes: Walk the Park Street corridor to the library for catalog access, reading and research resources, or a listed community program.
cards.short_summary: A public library stop with resources and programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Canton Free Library lists its address as 8 Park Street and offers catalog access, programs, and research resources.
cards.source_title: Canton Free Library
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Monday–Friday 9 AM–6 PM; Saturday 10 AM–3 PM.

cards.title: See period rooms and local history
cards.subtitle: East Main Street corridor — 3 E. Main Street
cards.notes: Follow East Main Street to tour historic rooms, galleries, the children’s attic, and the research room at this history center.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic-house museum with local collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The center identifies the Silas Wright House & Museum at 3 E. Main Street and describes historic rooms, galleries, a children’s attic, and a research room.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — St. Lawrence County Center for History and Culture
cards.access_notes: Museum tours are listed Tuesday–Saturday, 10 AM–4 PM, March–December; admission is $5 for non-members.

cards.title: Look for a hands-on arts workshop
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 53 Main Street
cards.notes: Stop on Main Street to check TAUNY’s current calendar for hands-on workshops and other traditional-arts programming.
cards.short_summary: A traditional-arts center with workshops in downtown Canton.
cards.evidence_claim: TAUNY lists hands-on workshops at the TAUNY Center, 53 Main Street, Canton.
cards.source_title: TAUNY
cards.access_notes: Check TAUNY’s event calendar for registration requirements and workshop pricing.

cards.title: Browse maps, books, and outdoor gear
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 45 Main Street
cards.notes: Use this Main Street stop to browse the shop’s maps, books, outdoor gear, apparel, or ask about bike and ski service.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor-gear shop with maps and books.
cards.evidence_claim: Grasse River Outfitters lists its Canton location at 45 Main Street and identifies maps, books, outdoor gear, bike service, and ski tuning.
cards.source_title: Grasse River Outfitters
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases and service availability vary; confirm current offerings with the shop.

cards.title: Pick up a vegetarian or vegan lunch
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 21 Main Street
cards.notes: Head along Main Street for the store’s listed vegetarian and vegan prepared-food options, including soups, sushi, wraps, and grab-and-go lunches.
cards.short_summary: A natural-food store with prepared vegetarian and vegan options.
cards.evidence_claim: Nature’s Storehouse lists 21 Main Street, Canton and describes daily vegetarian and vegan options including soup, sushi, wraps, and grab-and-go lunches.
cards.source_title: Nature's Storehouse
cards.access_notes: Listed store hours are Monday–Friday 9 AM–6 PM and Saturday–Sunday 9 AM–5 PM.

cards.title: Choose a listed downtown meal stop
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 31 Main Street
cards.notes: Use Main Street for a sit-down meal at Sergi’s; SUNY Canton’s current local dining page lists the restaurant and address.
cards.short_summary: A named Main Street restaurant listed by a neighboring university.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Canton lists Sergi’s Italian Restaurant at 31 Main Street in Canton.
cards.source_title: SUNY Canton — Hotels & Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Restaurant access and current service details should be confirmed directly before visiting.

cards.title: Add an East Main lunch option
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 43 Main Street
cards.notes: Keep this independently named restaurant in mind while walking Main Street; it is listed on SUNY Canton’s local dining page.
cards.short_summary: A named Main Street restaurant in Canton’s local dining listings.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Canton lists A-1 Oriental Kitchen at 43 Main Street in Canton.
cards.source_title: SUNY Canton — Hotels & Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Restaurant access and current service details should be confirmed directly before visiting.

cards.title: Find the Canton bakery and coffee counter
cards.subtitle: East Main Street corridor — 103 Main Street
cards.notes: Continue east on Main Street to the company’s Canton location for its bakery and coffee-counter offerings.
cards.short_summary: A company-listed Canton bakery and coffee location.
cards.evidence_claim: Park Bros. identifies its Canton, New York location as 103 Main Street.
cards.source_title: Park Bros. Bagels & Coffee
cards.access_notes: Purchase is required; verify current counter hours directly with Park Bros.

cards.title: Plan for the seasonal market
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor — Village Green Park, 17 Park Street at Main Street
cards.notes: Time a Park Street walk for the state-listed Friday market season, held at Village Green Park at the Main Street corner.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal farmers’ market at Village Green Park.
cards.evidence_claim: New York State lists the Canton Friday Farmers’ Market at Village Green Park, 17 Park Street at Main Street, Fridays from May 9 through October 31.
cards.source_title: New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets — Farmers' Market Schedules
cards.access_notes: State schedule lists Fridays, 9 AM–2 PM, May 9–October 31; confirm the current season before going.

cards.title: Use the park as a downtown reset point
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor — beside East Main Street
cards.notes: Make the named village park your outdoor pause on the Park Street corridor, then continue toward the library and Main Street destinations.
cards.short_summary: A documented public park in Canton’s downtown park network.
cards.evidence_claim: A Village and Town of Canton planning document identifies Canton Village Park among the community’s parks.
cards.source_title: Canton Brownfield Opportunity Area Designation Package
cards.access_notes: Public-park access is generally outdoor; check village notices for event-related restrictions.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented St. Lawrence traditions spanning first-year welcome, academic milestones, outdoor activity, performance, and campus history.

cards.title: Light a candle on your first night
cards.subtitle: First-year welcome tradition
cards.notes: Attend the first-year gathering, hear the president’s address, and join the ceremonial candle lighting that marks the start of your Laurentian experience.
cards.short_summary: A first-night ceremony built around the University’s “candle in the wilderness” symbol.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence says first-year students gather on their first night for a presidential address and ceremonial candle lighting symbolizing the candle in the wilderness.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of first-year arrival programming; confirm the current orientation schedule.

cards.title: Move up a pew in Gunnison Chapel
cards.subtitle: Academic recognition ceremony
cards.notes: Watch the class ahead leave its pews, then take the newly opened row as the ceremony recognizes academic and co-curricular achievement.
cards.short_summary: Students literally advance a row of pews as their class progresses.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Moving-Up Day as a tradition since 1869 in which students move up a row of pews in Gunnison Memorial Chapel and new Omicron Delta Kappa members are tapped.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Ceremony timing is set by the University; follow official academic-year announcements.

cards.title: Begin with the incoming class
cards.subtitle: First-year class welcome
cards.notes: Join your entering class and families for the formal welcome that marks the official start of study at St. Lawrence.
cards.short_summary: A formal first gathering that welcomes the new class to the Laurentian community.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence identifies Matriculation as the tradition that officially welcomes first-year students and families and symbolizes the official start of their St. Lawrence experience.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Held during first-year arrival; consult official move-in and orientation communications.

cards.title: Represent your FYP team
cards.subtitle: Semester-long first-year competition
cards.notes: Take part with your team through lawn games, trivia, campus events, readings, presentations, and the songwriting contest to earn points.
cards.short_summary: First-year teams collect points across a semester of activities and campus engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the First-Year Cup is a semester-long competition featuring lawn games, trivia, a songwriting contest, and points for attending campus events, readings, and presentations.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: For first-year participants; activity dates and team details are announced through the First-Year Program.

cards.title: Mark 100 nights to commencement
cards.subtitle: Senior-class chapel gathering
cards.notes: Gather with the senior class in Gunnison Memorial Chapel 100 nights before commencement to reflect on shared years at St. Lawrence.
cards.short_summary: A senior gathering that counts down to commencement through reflection in the chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence says the senior class gathers in Gunnison Memorial Chapel 100 nights before commencement to reflect on their years together.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Senior-class event; the date follows the University commencement calendar.

cards.title: Hike a High Peak with the Outing Club
cards.subtitle: Adirondack fall tradition
cards.notes: Register through the Outing Club for a group hike in Adirondack Park; choose a route matching your preparation and follow trip-leader guidance.
cards.short_summary: Students spread across the Adirondacks to put a Laurentian on each of the 46 High Peaks.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence says Peak Weekend sends students of varying hiking experience into Adirondack Park each fall to pursue High Peaks, with at least one Laurentian on each of 46 summits.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor activity requires advance coordination, appropriate gear, and adherence to Outing Club trip guidance.

cards.title: Watch skiing and snowboarding on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Brush Memorial Quad winter event
cards.notes: Visit Brush Memorial Quad during the event to watch students ski and snowboard on the rail built there by the Outing Club.
cards.short_summary: The Outing Club brings a ski-and-snowboard rail to the central campus quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that for Rail Jam, the Outing Club builds a rail on Brush Memorial Quad where students ski and snowboard on campus.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Seasonal event; attend or participate only through current Outing Club and University event guidance.

cards.title: Share in Kaleidoscope performances
cards.subtitle: International House spring celebration
cards.notes: Attend the spring program at International House to experience music, dance, poetry, and other performances celebrating campus diversity and inclusion.
cards.short_summary: A spring I-House performance celebration founded by a St. Lawrence international student.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence says Kaleidoscope was founded in 2006 by Victor Kai-Rogers ’08 and is hosted by International House each spring with music, dance, poetry, and more.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Spring event; check International House and University event listings for the current program.

cards.title: Meet North Country makers and musicians
cards.subtitle: Green House seasonal gathering
cards.notes: Look for the Green House invitation when spring arrives, then spend time with regional craftspeople and musicians sharing their work on campus.
cards.short_summary: A Green House gathering that highlights regional crafts and music as winter gives way to spring.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the Green House invites regional craftspeople and musicians to Folk Fest to share their work and highlight North Country cultural traditions.
cards.source_title: Traditions and Special Events | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Seasonal event; check University and Green House announcements for current details.

cards.title: Pause for the weekday chime
cards.subtitle: Campus bell-ringing tradition
cards.notes: Listen near campus at 5 p.m. on an academic-year weekday for the Bacheller Memorial Chime, donated by alumnus and author Irving Bacheller.
cards.short_summary: A 1926 chime continues to ring on academic-year weekdays at 5 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence’s history states that the Bacheller Memorial Chime was donated in 1926 and that its bells ring every weekday during the academic year at 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Mission and History | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: The University states the bells ring on academic-year weekdays at 5 p.m.; schedules may vary during breaks.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at St Lawrence University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence built around campus landmarks, first-year activities, food, reflection, and shared time.

cards.title: Start at the Sullivan Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival • student hub
cards.notes: Use the Information Desk as a practical first stop, then find the lounge and meeting areas so you know where student programming and services are based.
cards.short_summary: Orient yourself in the campus’s central student space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sullivan Student Center provides student study, lounge, meeting, event, dining, mail, and Student Life spaces.
cards.source_title: Sullivan Student Center | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Student spaces and room use are subject to University access and reservation policies.

cards.title: Have your first campus dinner at Dana
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • campus dining
cards.notes: Meet a classmate for a meal and look over the dining setup together; Dana serves buffet-style meals and lists daily menus through Dining Services.
cards.short_summary: A straightforward first shared meal on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Dana is St. Lawrence’s main dining hall, open seven days a week, with buffet-style meals and daily menu information.
cards.source_title: Dining | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Meals are obtained through a meal plan or guest payment; check current Dining Services information.

cards.title: Pause at Gunnison Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • campus landmark
cards.notes: Walk through the chapel grounds and save a moment for quiet reflection. Check the campus calendar before entering for an event or gathering.
cards.short_summary: A historic place for a calm first-night reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Gunnison Memorial Chapel opened in 1926 and serves campus and community gatherings; student bell ringers play its bells on weekdays during classes.
cards.source_title: Gunnison Memorial Chapel History and Photos | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Gathering and event access varies; consult the Chaplain’s Office or campus calendar.

cards.title: See Herring-Cole Hall in daylight
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • historic campus
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk to this historic building and, when available, settle into the Cole Reading Room for quiet reading or individual desk work.
cards.short_summary: Pair a campus walk with a historic reading room.
cards.evidence_claim: Herring-Cole Hall is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Cole Reading Room is designated for quiet study during the academic year.
cards.source_title: 360-Degree Campus Tours | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: The Cole Reading Room is for individual desk work and reading; observe posted building access rules.

cards.title: Make Owen D. Young Library your study anchor
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning • library stop
cards.notes: Find a study floor, then note the ground-floor meditation and prayer space for a quiet break between orientation tasks and new conversations.
cards.short_summary: Locate a reliable academic and quiet-space resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Owen D. Young Library has a ground-floor space with meditation cushions and prayer mats that students may use for breathing, meditation, and Muslim prayer.
cards.source_title: Wellness Zones | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Library access and services may vary by academic calendar and campus ID status.

cards.title: Look for the current Brush Art Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • campus art
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition information before you go, then use the visit as an easy conversation starter with a new friend or roommate.
cards.short_summary: See rotating art on campus and take in a visual change of pace.
cards.evidence_claim: The Richard F. Brush Art Gallery is on campus and has a permanent collection of more than 7,000 objects alongside regularly rotating exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Art and Art History | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Confirm current exhibition dates and gallery access before visiting.

cards.title: Take a breather in the North Country Garden
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • Sykes Hall courtyard
cards.notes: Bring a water bottle or a book and use the garden for a short reset. It is intended as a quiet outdoor place to sit, eat, meditate, or study.
cards.short_summary: A designated campus spot for a gentle outdoor pause.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence identifies the North Country Garden near Sykes Hall as an outdoor space students may use to sit, meditate, eat lunch, or study.
cards.source_title: Wellness Zones | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use depends on weather and normal campus access conditions.

cards.title: Join a First-Year Cup activity
cards.subtitle: Saturday • first-year tradition
cards.notes: Ask your First-Year Program or resident staff what Cup activity is next, then join the option that feels comfortable—games, trivia, banner making, or songs.
cards.short_summary: A school-specific way to meet peers during the opening days.
cards.evidence_claim: First-Year Cup begins in students’ first days on campus and includes lawn games, trivia, banner-designing, and song competition.
cards.source_title: First-Year Program | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Participation details and timing are set by the First-Year Program each semester.

cards.title: Pick a Backyard Adventure
cards.subtitle: Saturday • first-week group outing
cards.notes: Choose a listed group outing that suits your energy and access needs. The program includes options such as hiking, screen-printing, pottery, escape rooms, and apple picking.
cards.short_summary: A structured way to explore the North Country with new people.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence’s First-Year Program describes Backyard Adventures as first-week group outings including screen-printing, escape rooms, hiking, pottery, virtual reality, ropes courses, and apple picking.
cards.source_title: First-Year Program | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Offerings, registration, transportation, and any fees vary by outing; confirm with the First-Year Program.

cards.title: Close with a Shared Sunday activity
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon • connect beyond class
cards.notes: Check the week’s Shared Sunday plans and bring a friend. Choose a relaxed activity such as board games, crocheting, canoeing, or hiking if offered.
cards.short_summary: End the weekend with a low-pressure shared activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Shared Sunday invites students, faculty, and staff to Sunday-afternoon activities including canoeing, hiking, board games, and crocheting.
cards.source_title: First-Year Program | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Activities and availability vary; consult First-Year Program communications for the current schedule.
